label: ledger-iter3
brand: the Ledger fixture's own identity: a warm-paper fintech dashboard in the Mercury/Anthropic lane — ivory paper, one clay accent, serif numbers-as-headlines, small tool-like radii, light-first

defects: Transaction table row padding too tight; subtitle text nearly touches the row boundary, breaking the calm vertical rhythm the rest of the page maintains
Right edge of the cash-flow chart section header is clipped: '– Out $40.7k · – Set $6.7k' runs into the viewport edge with no gutter, a hard alignment break
The disclosure section at the bottom uses a heavy beige box that feels visually weightier than the rest of the page's calm density — it anchors too much attention to footer fine print
Chart legend (net / inflow / outflow) is left-aligned beneath a right-side scrubber label; the dual alignment competes and muddles the reading order
Section eyebrows ('OVERVIEW', 'CASH FLOW · 90 DAYS') use very small, wide-tracked caps that strain at WCAG minimums; they read as texture more than label in a quick-scan pass
improvements: Widen row padding in the transactions table to restore calm density
Fix right-gutter clipping on the cash-flow section header
Reduce visual weight of the disclosures container so it recedes

critiques.label: The company's money, in plain figures
defects: The eyebrow 'OVERVIEW' is clipped at the top viewport edge, breaking the calm, intentional framing.
The large chart's x-axis labels and gridlines are entirely missing, forcing users to guess temporal values.
The 'In, out, and the net between' heading has weak vertical breathing room directly above the chart container.
The delta chips use two different background tints (pale green vs pale red) which fragments the 'disciplined' color system.
The footnote and legend at the very bottom feel visually disconnected and cramped against the viewport's lower boundary.
improvements: Restore top padding to prevent the clipped 'OVERVIEW' eyebrow text.
Add subtle x-axis date ticks to the chart for actual data orientation.
Increase vertical spacing between section headings and their corresponding data blocks.

critiques.label: In, out, and the net between
defects: Horizontal misalignment: The '30 Oct 2026' timestamp is not vertically aligned with the 'In, out, and...' headline baseline.
Spacing Rhythm: The gap between the 'SCRUB DAYS' slider and the 'Y-axis clamps' footnote is too large compared to the slider-to-label gap.
Color Contrast: The light gray 'STATUS' column header has insufficient contrast against the off-white background for WCAG AA.
Visual Noise: The red line chart peaks are jagged and cluttered, competing visually with the clean serif typography below.
Inconsistent Labels: 'CASH FLOW' and 'TRANSACTIONS' use all-caps tracking that feels too tight for the 'warm-paper' brand lane.
improvements: Align top-right metadata baselines with the main section headline.
Reduce whitespace between the scrub slider and y-axis footnote.
Increase font weight for status column headers to improve contrast.

critiques.label: Where it went
defects: Typographic scale is fractured: 'Where it went' headline is identical weight/size to column headers, failing to establish visual hierarchy.
Merchant sub-labels (e.g., 'Infrastructure', 'Payroll') are too small and low-contrast to read comfortably, violating accessibility standards.
The clay accent color is underutilized; only the 'pending' and 'failed' status pills use it, leaving the rest of the table feeling monochrome and dull.
Row height is inconsistent; some rows have more whitespace than others, breaking the visual rhythm and creating a 'jagged' edge to the table.
improvements: Increase 'Where it went' size and weight to 24px/600 to dominate the section.
Boost sub-label contrast to #6B7280 and size to 13px for legibility.
Apply subtle clay left-borders to settled rows to inject brand warmth.

critiques.label: Four buckets, one position
defects: Vertical spacing between the transaction table and 'Four buckets, one position' header is excessively large
Account cards lack clear visual affordance, making interactive state ambiguous
'DISCLOSURES' section header uses excessive horizontal spacing, reducing readability
Footer text 'Just typography' is cut off, suggesting a layout or alignment error
Account card numbers are not visually distinct enough from labels, weakening hierarchy
improvements: Reduce gap between table and section headers
Add subtle hover states to account cards
Increase disclosure section spacing for readability

critiques.label: The fine print, on purpose
defects: Serif numerals only apply to card amounts, not headline 'Four buckets' or table headers, breaking the brand's 'numbers-as-headlines' rule.
Footer 'Read the build contract' link uses the clay accent on near-white with a thin underline, sitting just under AA contrast for small text.
Three disclosure paragraphs are set in the same voice and scale as card subtitles, so 'fine print' reads as body copy rather than legal disclaimers.
Section gaps between ledger table, ACCOUNTS, and DISCLOSURES are uneven; the 48px jump above 'Four buckets' feels looser than the 32px jump above 'DISCLOSURES'.
Card masks '9417 •••• 3382' all use identical monospace size as the dollar figure below the title, flattening hierarchy inside each card.
improvements: Set 'Four buckets, one position' in the serif numerals face at 32px.
Bump disclosure body to 13px/1.6 in muted gray-600, keep 'DISCLOSURES' at 11px caps.
Unify vertical rhythm to 40px between all three major bands.

defects: The 'CASH FLOW - 90 DAYS' section header is partially cut off on the left side, revealing a missing or overlapping container edge.
The 4 metric cards at the top use varying vertical baselines for their sub-text (e.g., '4 accounts...' vs '90-day series...') creating visual noise in the grid.
The scrubber slider control appears too small for comfortable desktop interaction, reducing discoverability of the interactive element.
The chart's Y-axis labels are extremely faint and positioned arbitrarily, failing to provide clear scale reference for the cash-flow line.
The 'failed' status badge for Delta Air Lines relies solely on color (pink) and low-contrast text, lacking the clarity of the green 'settled' badges.
improvements: Fix left-aligned section headers and remove the stray vertical border artifact at the cash-flow container start.
Standardize vertical alignment of all card sub-text and increase scrubber slider visual affordance for precise desktop control.
Increase contrast on chart Y-axis labels and failed-status badges to improve readability without compromising the warm-paper aesthetic.

defects: Cash flow chart: x-axis labels are completely obscured/missing, only a red cursor dot is visible against a blank background, making the time-series data unreadable.
Transactions table: right-aligned AMOUNT column text ('-$4,8...', '$120,...') is heavily truncated or cut off, destroying the financial data integrity.
Runway card: The delta chip on other cards is absent here, creating a visual asymmetry in the card grid; the card feels 'looser' than the others.
Header: 'Open an account' CTA button is extremely wide and visually heavy compared to the sparse, minimalist logo on the left.
Footer: 'Not a bank... Just typography' text is small and low-contrast, fading into the background.
improvements: Add a placeholder state to the Runway card to match the delta chip layout of peers.

critiques.label: The company's money, in plain figures
defects: The 'Annualized Revenue' card is cut off at the bottom viewport, creating an awkward crop on the largest value in the set.
Meta text (e.g., '4 accounts...') feels visually isolated and disconnected from the KPI card's internal grouping.
Using the same serif face for the large KPI numbers and the headline dilutes the intended 'data vs. content' typographic distinction.
improvements: Add bottom padding or viewport-safe cropping to prevent the last card from being sliced.
Introduce a subtle horizontal rule or increased vertical gap between KPI values and their metadata.
Switch KPI figures to a monospaced typeface to reinforce the 'Ledger' data aesthetic.

critiques.label: In, out, and the net between
defects: The vertical gap between the 'SCRUB DAYS' control block and the 'Y-axis clamps' footnote is too large, breaking the card's internal rhythm and feeling like wasted whitespace.
The serif headline 'In, out, and the net between' has an awkwardly tight right-margin on mobile, nearly cropping the 'n' which undermines the careful 'tool-like' precision of the layout.
The legend at the bottom of the chart card uses small, thin lines paired with very small text, making the 'outflow' vs 'inflow' distinction difficult to parse quickly.
The 'TRANSACTIONS · THIS MONTH' overline and the massive 'Where it went' headline below it create a competing visual weight that disrupts the calm density of the section.
The horizontal scrolling of the table header ('AMOUN' is cut off) combined with the large empty space to the right of the '$' values suggests a layout that isn't optimized for mobile read-lines.
improvements: Tighten the vertical rhythm between the scrub control and the chart footnote to ensure consistent 8px spacing cadence.
improvements_secondary: Increase the legend line thickness and font weight for immediate visual parsing of data series.
improvements_tertiary: Reduce the gap between the transaction overline and its headline to improve visual cohesion.

critiques.label: Where it went
defects: The 'AMOUN' header is truncated, breaking the table's data legibility and professional polish at the right edge.
The secondary row label 'seeded fixture' beneath '12 rows' is faint and competes functionally with the primary row-count data, muddying the metadata hierarchy.
The semantic color coding for revenue (green) and expense (dark) is applied, but the specific shade of green '$120,' against the ivory background is borderline for WCAG AA contrast on small text.
The 'Amount' column's right-aligned currency figures lack visible container padding on the right, causing the numbers to sit too close to the edge on mobile viewports.
improvements: Widen the table container or abbreviate the header to 'AMOUNT' to prevent the text truncation at the right edge.
Increase font weight of 'seeded fixture' or move it to a muted icon to establish a cleaner metadata hierarchy.
Add 8px right padding to the amount column to give the currency figures intentional breathing room.

critiques.label: Four buckets, one position
defects: Section title “Four buckets” sits too close to the small overline; no breathing room above the heading
Monetary figures and masked card numbers use identical 16px scale, letting card data compete with balance hierarchy
Card internal padding feels slightly cramped on the right, creating visual strain before the rounded border edge
Vertical rhythm between eyebrow and H2 lacks a deliberate gap, weakening the typographic cadence of the band
Masked card suffix is the same gray as descriptive copy, reducing legibility of the identifier detail
improvements: Increase top margin before section title for calm entry
Increase font size on monetary balances to 20px or 24px
Increase vertical gap between account labels and their sub-descriptions

critiques.label: The fine print, on purpose
defects: The clay border around the 'DISCLOSURES' card is too thick and creates a noisy, unrefined boundary that breaks the minimalist 'warm-paper' aesthetic.
The footer text 'Ledger - a design fixture...' lacks visual hierarchy; it is rendered in the same gray as the card body copy, failing to establish a clear end-of-section marker.
The gap between the main card and the footer is excessively large, creating a dead zone that disrupts the vertical rhythm established by the tighter spacing within the card.
The 'Tax' card at the top feels disconnected; the transition from the card content to the 'DISCLOSURES' section lacks a logical visual bridge.
Serif numerals in '$366,800' are bold but the font weight difference against the sans-serif labels feels jarring rather than elegant.
improvements: Reduce the card border thickness to 1px and switch to a soft, low-contrast hairline stroke.
Increase footer top margin to tighten the vertical rhythm and establish a clear visual anchor.
Use a slightly bolder weight for footer labels to distinguish them from body text.
